key_insight: An AI-assisted workflow could feasibly screen discharge summaries for potential treatment injury and help surface cases for clinician review that might otherwise be missed.
clinical_relevance: This approach may improve detection of inpatient harm signals and support follow-up for possible ACC consideration, but it is not a stand-alone diagnostic tool.
method: Single-site, 6-month pilot at Wairarapa Hospital using an LLM to screen 2,642 inpatient discharge summaries
The model produced structured candidate harm signals with supporting text and certainty labels
Clinicians reviewed all flagged cases and decided whether escalation was warranted
evidence_signal: The system flagged 237 summaries (9.0% yield), with 43.0% confirmed iatrogenic harm PPV and 61.2% when possible harm was included; 4.6% of outputs were unsupported.
watch_item: Performance was assessed without an independent chart-review reference standard, so accuracy, equity, and generalisability still need prospective validation.
paper_title: AI-assisted identification of potential treatment injury from inpatient discharge summaries: an early-stage sociotechnical evaluation in a New Zealand district hospital
